questions.question: Which group of verbs is typical academic vocabulary for analysis?
questions.explanation: Academic analysis verbs include analyse, evaluate, assess, compare, contrast, examine and interpret.

questions.question: Which word means "therefore" and is used to draw conclusions in academic texts?
questions.explanation: "Consequently" and "therefore" signal conclusions. "However" signals contrast and "meanwhile" signals time.

questions.question: What is the difference between "furthermore" and "however"?
options: "Furthermore" adds a supporting point; "however" introduces a contrast
questions.explanation: "Furthermore" and "moreover" add more support, while "however" and "nevertheless" introduce contrasting ideas.

questions.question: In an academic task, what does "evaluate" ask you to do?
options: Judge the value or quality of something, weighing strengths and weaknesses
Copy the text into your answer
questions.explanation: To evaluate means to judge the value of something - considering strengths, weaknesses and evidence before reaching a conclusion.

questions.question: Why is subject-specific vocabulary useful across school subjects?
options: It lets you understand and discuss topics precisely in science, history and other subjects
It is only needed for spelling tests
It makes texts harder to understand on purpose
questions.explanation: Each subject has key terms (e.g. hypothesis in science, democracy in social studies), and knowing them lets you read and write precisely in that subject.
